label: Schema reference
requiredWhen: Optional editor hint, never an authority or executable resource.
what: An editor reference to the project JSON schema.
why: Editors can offer completion; the bundled core still enforces its own versioned policy.
where: Use the schema shipped with your selected toolkit revision.
format: An absolute URI of at most 2048 characters. The app never fetches this URI.
failure: An invalid URI is rejected; a valid URI does not change the validator.

label: Configuration version
requiredWhen: Always required; exactly 1.
what: The release configuration contract version.
why: Unknown versions must not be interpreted using different policy.
where: This toolkit uses configuration schema version 1.
format: The integer 1, not a string or boolean.
failure: Any other version is rejected.

label: Committed version file
requiredWhen: Always required.
what: The project file containing the release version and build number.
why: One committed source must agree with the effective app and retained artifacts.
where: Choose your existing version properties or xcconfig file inside the project.
format: A slash-separated repository-relative path, at most 512 characters; no dot traversal or backslashes.
failure: Draft validation checks the path syntax only, not file existence or version values.

label: Marketing version key
requiredWhen: Always required.
what: The property naming the public app version.
why: Keeps display versions consistent across the selected platforms.
where: Read the uppercase key in your committed version file.
format: Uppercase letter followed by uppercase letters, digits or underscores; at most 64 characters.
failure: A missing or invalid key blocks later version validation; the draft check does not read the file.

label: Build number key
requiredWhen: Always required.
what: The property naming the committed numeric build.
why: Build-once promotion must keep the exact same positive build number.
where: Read the build key in your committed version file.
format: An uppercase configuration key, at most 64 characters. Later checks require a canonical positive integer from 1 to 2100000000.
failure: An invalid key or later noncanonical build blocks release validation.

label: Candidate branch
requiredWhen: Always required.
what: The branch allowed to produce a new candidate.
why: Protected workflows must bind dispatch policy to actual observed source.
where: Use the reviewed branch name in your GitHub repository.
format: A safe Git branch name of at most 255 characters, without refs/heads/ unless that is your actual branch policy.
failure: Syntax alone does not prove branch protection, a clean checkout or dispatch permission.

label: Production branch
requiredWhen: Always required.
what: The branch allowed to prepare production from authentic predecessor evidence.
why: Protected workflows must bind dispatch policy to actual observed source.
where: Use the reviewed branch name in your GitHub repository.
format: A safe Git branch name of at most 255 characters, without refs/heads/ unless that is your actual branch policy.
failure: Syntax alone does not prove branch protection, a clean checkout or dispatch permission.

label: Private dependency access
requiredWhen: Set true only if a candidate build needs explicitly selected private dependency access.
what: Whether application builds require a read-only project dependency token.
why: Public preflight defers compilation rather than giving project code ambient account credentials.
where: Confirm the minimal access needed for your private project dependencies.
format: Boolean. Omission uses false. Never put the token value in configuration.
failure: A required token must be provided through the future protected credential flow; it never grants Store authority.

label: Android release
requiredWhen: Always required; at least one platform must be enabled.
what: Whether this platform participates in the release.
why: Disabled platforms must not accidentally receive credentials or Store actions.
where: Select the app platforms this project is intended to release.
format: Boolean. A disabled section must contain only enabled=false.
failure: Both platforms disabled, or extra fields on a disabled section, are invalid.

label: Application ID
requiredWhen: Required when android.enabled is true.
what: The stable public identity of the application.
why: Artifacts and Store targets must match the intended application exactly.
where: Compare the release project settings with the existing Store app identity.
format: A dotted Android application ID; at most 255 characters.
failure: A discovered string is only an unverified hint; later project/artifact/Store checks must agree.

label: Android identity approval
requiredWhen: Required when android.enabled is true.
what: Your explicit policy decision about the proposed app identity.
why: Discovery must never approve an identity merely because it found a matching string.
where: An owner reviews the real application, signing identity and Store record.
format: Choose unverified, approved or blocked. Approved also requires the platform Store/signing policy fields.
failure: Approved is configured policy, not native or service verification. Blocked prevents release activation.

label: iOS release
requiredWhen: Always required; at least one platform must be enabled.
what: Whether this platform participates in the release.
why: Disabled platforms must not accidentally receive credentials or Store actions.
where: Select the app platforms this project is intended to release.
format: Boolean. A disabled section must contain only enabled=false.
failure: Both platforms disabled, or extra fields on a disabled section, are invalid.

label: Bundle ID
requiredWhen: Required when ios.enabled is true.
what: The stable public identity of the application.
why: Artifacts and Store targets must match the intended application exactly.
where: Compare the release project settings with the existing Store app identity.
format: A dotted bundle ID using letters, digits and hyphens; at most 255 characters.
failure: A discovered string is only an unverified hint; later project/artifact/Store checks must agree.

label: iOS identity approval
requiredWhen: Required when ios.enabled is true.
what: Your explicit policy decision about the proposed app identity.
why: Discovery must never approve an identity merely because it found a matching string.
where: An owner reviews the real application, signing identity and Store record.
format: Choose unverified, approved or blocked. Approved also requires the platform Store/signing policy fields.
failure: Approved is configured policy, not native or service verification. Blocked prevents release activation.

label: Android application module
requiredWhen: Explicit selection is needed when static discovery has multiple application modules.
what: The Gradle application module to build.
why: Prevents a library, sample or unrelated application from being selected.
where: Use the application module path declared by your Gradle settings.
format: A colon-delimited Gradle module path of at most 512 characters; : selects the root project.
failure: Ambiguous or mismatched selection needs owner review and later effective Gradle validation.

label: Android release variant
requiredWhen: Optional; the existing core defaults to release.
what: The application variant used by the release build.
why: Flavors and suffixes can change the effective app identity and signing behavior.
where: Review your Gradle build types/flavors and intended release variant.
format: A letter followed by letters, digits, underscore or hyphen; at most 128 characters.
failure: A valid string does not prove the variant exists or builds.

label: External testing track
requiredWhen: Required inside externalTrack; externalTrack is required for an approved Android identity.
what: The exact configured Play testing-track name.
why: External testing promotes the original candidate build while preserving unrelated releases.
where: Copy the testing track from Play Console after its testing setup is complete.
format: Nonempty text of at most 100 characters; internal and production are forbidden.
failure: Missing or inconsistent track policy blocks activation; this draft check does not query Play.

label: Testing-track type
requiredWhen: Required whenever android.externalTrack is present.
what: Whether the selected track is closed or open testing.
why: Each type has a distinct guarded Store contract.
where: Check the track type in Play Console.
format: closed or open. Closed testing requires supported, verifiable Google Group assignment.
failure: A configured type is not proof that tester access is usable.

label: Android upload certificate
requiredWhen: Required when Android identityStatus is approved.
what: The SHA-256 fingerprint of the intended upload certificate.
why: A signed artifact must use the approved upload identity.
where: Obtain the public certificate fingerprint from your upload key and compare with Play App Integrity.
format: Exactly 64 hexadecimal characters, no separators; all-zero placeholders are forbidden.
failure: Syntax validity does not prove possession of the key or Store acceptance. Never paste a private key here.

label: App Store numeric app ID
requiredWhen: Required when iOS identityStatus is approved.
what: The numeric App Store Connect record identifier.
why: Store operations must select the exact existing app, not a name match.
where: Copy Apple ID from the app information page in App Store Connect.
format: A string of 1 to 20 decimal digits.
failure: Format validation does not prove access to this app.

label: Apple developer team
requiredWhen: Required when iOS identityStatus is approved.
what: The Apple Developer Team ID used for signing.
why: Profiles, certificates, entitlements and app identity must bind to the intended team.
where: Copy Team ID from your Apple Developer membership details.
format: Exactly 10 uppercase letters or digits.
failure: A matching format does not establish certificate/profile authorization.

label: Xcode project
requiredWhen: Use one explicit container when discovery is ambiguous; project and workspace are mutually exclusive.
what: The Xcode container used for the iOS app.
why: A reproducible build must select the intended app rather than an arbitrary discovered container.
where: Select the existing .xcodeproj path inside your project.
format: A repository-relative path of at most 512 characters, using forward slashes.
failure: Selecting both project and workspace is invalid; draft checks do not open Xcode.

label: Xcode workspace
requiredWhen: Use one explicit container when discovery is ambiguous; project and workspace are mutually exclusive.
what: The Xcode container used for the iOS app.
why: A reproducible build must select the intended app rather than an arbitrary discovered container.
where: Select the existing .xcworkspace path inside your project.
format: A repository-relative path of at most 512 characters, using forward slashes.
failure: Selecting both project and workspace is invalid; draft checks do not open Xcode.

label: Shared Xcode scheme
requiredWhen: Explicit selection is needed when no single shared scheme is discoverable.
what: The app scheme used for archive creation.
why: The scheme chooses targets and archive behavior.
where: Use a checked-in shared scheme for the selected Xcode container.
format: Nonempty single-line text of at most 255 characters.
failure: Static discovery cannot prove that the scheme archives successfully.

label: Archive configuration
requiredWhen: Optional; the existing core defaults to Release.
what: The Xcode build configuration for archives.
why: Release settings, identities and version values must be deliberate.
where: Review the selected scheme and project build configurations.
format: Nonempty single-line text of at most 255 characters.
failure: A configured name does not establish a usable native Xcode toolchain.

label: Project preparation command
requiredWhen: Use only when your project needs an explicitly reviewed preparation step.
what: A project-owned argument vector for generating or preparing iOS inputs.
why: Generation stays in the application-side trust boundary, never a Store-authorized job.
where: Provide the existing reviewed project script and arguments; do not paste shell syntax.
format: A JSON array of 1–64 nonempty string arguments, each at most 4096 characters.
failure: This foundation never executes it. Later execution needs the guarded core flow; shell substitution is forbidden.

label: External TestFlight group
requiredWhen: Required when iOS identityStatus is approved.
what: The exact external testing group to receive the candidate build.
why: Only verified available-to-testers evidence makes later production eligible.
where: Copy the external group name from App Store Connect TestFlight.
format: Nonempty single-line text of at most 255 characters.
failure: A group name does not prove membership, review approval or tester availability.

label: Apple distribution certificate
requiredWhen: Required when iOS identityStatus is approved.
what: The SHA-256 fingerprint of the intended distribution certificate.
why: Signing material and the exported artifact must match the selected identity.
where: Obtain the public fingerprint from your Apple Distribution certificate.
format: Exactly 64 hexadecimal characters, no separators; no all-zero placeholder.
failure: A configured fingerprint is not a validated P12, profile or signed artifact. Never paste private certificate material here.

label: iOS symbol policy
requiredWhen: Required inside symbols; symbols is required for an approved iOS identity.
what: Whether symbols are disabled, retained, or require a future guarded uploader.
why: Retained dSYMs support diagnosis and artifact correspondence checks.
where: Choose the policy appropriate for your release and symbol retention requirements.
format: disabled, retain or required. required is a fail-closed reserved activation sentinel, not an implemented uploader.
failure: Selecting required blocks release activation until guarded upload support exists; it does not silently upload.

label: Reserved symbol uploader
requiredWhen: Required only when symbols.policy is required; forbidden otherwise.
what: The reserved argument-vector contract for a future symbol integration.
why: An unimplemented uploader must never look like a completed release step.
where: Only document a reviewed future integration; no symbol uploader is enabled in this product scope.
format: A JSON argv array using the same bounded argument rules as project checks.
failure: The command is validated but never executed, including by existing release flows.

label: Non-exempt encryption
requiredWhen: Required inside review; review is required for an approved iOS identity.
what: Your reviewed declaration of the app encryption policy.
why: Apple review needs the correct compliance declaration for the actual app.
where: Review Apple export-compliance guidance and your app behavior with the responsible owner.
format: Explicit boolean; the toolkit does not make the legal determination for you.
failure: A valid boolean does not satisfy Apple agreements or legal obligations by itself.

label: Reviewer demo account
requiredWhen: Required inside review; review is required for an approved iOS identity.
what: Whether App Review needs a demo login.
why: Private reviewer access must be separate from public Store metadata.
where: Confirm the actual login requirements for testing your app.
format: Explicit boolean. Enter no username or password in this configuration.
failure: When true, later protected review flows require private demo credentials; they remain unknown here.

label: Store metadata folder
requiredWhen: Always required.
what: The project-relative root for public Store copy and images.
why: Metadata is reviewed, bounded and tied to the release evidence.
where: Use a dedicated public metadata tree in your project, not a private credential directory.
format: A slash-separated repository-relative path of at most 512 characters.
failure: Draft validation does not read metadata, screenshots, URLs or private reviewer values.

label: Android locales
requiredWhen: Always required as an array; nonempty while android is enabled.
what: The exact locales whose public metadata participates in this release.
why: Unconfigured Store localizations must not be overwritten or deleted.
where: Select the locale codes for the copy maintained under your metadata root.
format: A unique JSON array of locale strings, such as en-US or zh-Hans; disabled platforms may use [].
failure: Duplicates, malformed locales or an empty enabled-platform set are invalid; content is not checked here.

label: iOS locales
requiredWhen: Always required as an array; nonempty while ios is enabled.
what: The exact locales whose public metadata participates in this release.
why: Unconfigured Store localizations must not be overwritten or deleted.
where: Select the locale codes for the copy maintained under your metadata root.
format: A unique JSON array of locale strings, such as en-US or zh-Hans; disabled platforms may use [].
failure: Duplicates, malformed locales or an empty enabled-platform set are invalid; content is not checked here.

label: Android Firebase configuration
requiredWhen: Always required; use required only when this app depends on the corresponding client configuration.
what: The policy for providing a selected Firebase client configuration as a build input.
why: Build inputs must be selected and restored deliberately, not inherited from ambient private files.
where: Confirm whether your Android app needs google-services.json or GoogleService-Info.plist.
format: disabled or required. The private asset belongs in the future credential/import flow.
failure: required needs later material identity validation; this field is not proof that the file exists.

label: iOS Firebase configuration
requiredWhen: Always required; use required only when this app depends on the corresponding client configuration.
what: The policy for providing a selected Firebase client configuration as a build input.
why: Build inputs must be selected and restored deliberately, not inherited from ambient private files.
where: Confirm whether your iOS app needs google-services.json or GoogleService-Info.plist.
format: disabled or required. The private asset belongs in the future credential/import flow.
failure: required needs later material identity validation; this field is not proof that the file exists.

label: Preflight project checks
requiredWhen: Always required as an array; [] means no additional project-owned checks.
what: Explicit project-owned command argument vectors for this phase.
why: Application checks must never run with Store credentials or in the Store trust boundary.
where: Reviewed checks that belong before application compilation.
format: A JSON array of at most 32 argv arrays; each argv has 1–64 strings of at most 4096 characters. Only documented artifact placeholders are allowed.
failure: This foundation never executes commands. Invalid shell syntax or unsupported placeholders are rejected.

label: Android artifact checks
requiredWhen: Always required as an array; [] means no additional project-owned checks.
what: Explicit project-owned command argument vectors for this phase.
why: Application checks must never run with Store credentials or in the Store trust boundary.
where: Reviewed checks consuming the selected AAB artifact.
format: A JSON array of at most 32 argv arrays; each argv has 1–64 strings of at most 4096 characters. Only documented artifact placeholders are allowed.
failure: This foundation never executes commands. Invalid shell syntax or unsupported placeholders are rejected.

label: iOS artifact checks
requiredWhen: Always required as an array; [] means no additional project-owned checks.
what: Explicit project-owned command argument vectors for this phase.
why: Application checks must never run with Store credentials or in the Store trust boundary.
where: Reviewed checks consuming the selected IPA or dSYM artifacts.
format: A JSON array of at most 32 argv arrays; each argv has 1–64 strings of at most 4096 characters. Only documented artifact placeholders are allowed.
failure: This foundation never executes commands. Invalid shell syntax or unsupported placeholders are rejected.
